trim: LX (2.0L naturally aspirated I-4, M-CVT, FWD)

fields.note: Honda's 2024 Civic Sedan spec sheet lists a 107.7 in wheelbase for every trim; J.D. Power's 2024 Civic Sedan 4D LX page gives 'Wheelbase (in) 107.7'. TrueDelta's 2024 sedan listing also shows 107.7 in. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

iSeeCars' 2024 Civic dimensions page gives 'Front Track of 60.9 in' (the listing appears to be the EX sedan, not broken out for the LX). Auto123's 2025 Civic LX page gives 'Track Width, Front: 60.9 (in)'. No Honda track row surfaced in any summary; cars.com's 2024 LX page rounds to 61 in. Neither source is exactly a 2024 LX; treat as the generation's non-Si sedan figure. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

iSeeCars' 2024 Civic dimensions page gives 'Rear Track of 62.0 in' (listing appears to be the EX sedan). Auto123's 2025 Civic LX page gives 'Track Width, Rear: 62 (in)'; cars.com's 2024 LX page shows 62 in. No Honda track row surfaced. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Honda's 2024 Civic Sedan specifications list 184.0 in overall length; TrueDelta's 2024 sedan listing shows 'Length 184.0 in'. Yahoo's buyer's guide gives 179.0 in but covers sedan and hatchback together (see conflicts). Read from search-result summary; page not opened.
J.D. Power's 2024 Civic Sedan 4D LX spec page: width about 70.9 in without mirrors. No Honda width row surfaced in the summaries. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.
Height about 55.7 in per Honda's 2024 Civic Sedan specifications page; J.D. Power's 2024 LX sedan page gives the same. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Copied from the card research: LX column of Honda's 2024 Civic Sedan spec sheet, 2,877 lb (Sport 2,935, EX 3,004, Touring 3,077). This session's search: Edmunds gives 2,877 lbs and J.D. Power lists a base curb weight of 2,877 lbs for the LX. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Honda Information Center's 2024 Civic Sedan spec table lists weight distribution 61% front / 39% rear for the LX (same split for the Sport). Curb-weight basis, not with driver. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Copied from the card research: CarEdge's 2024 Civic LX page gives 5.3 in. No US Honda document listing ground clearance surfaced; Honda Canada's 2022 Civic Sedan sheet gives 134 mm no-load for the same generation, which is consistent. Other aggregators give 4.8 in and 4.4 in (see conflicts). Weak. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

fields.text: 2.0-liter (1,996 cc) naturally aspirated in-line 4-cylinder, 16-valve DOHC i-VTEC, multi-point fuel injection
fields.note: Copied from the card research: 2024 Civic Sedan spec sheet, LX/Sport engine 'In-Line 4-Cylinder, 1,996 cc, 16-Valve DOHC i-VTEC', multi-point injection. A motorreviewer.com result in this session identifies the Civic LX 2.0 as the K20C2. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.
Copied from the card research (fuelType): Honda sheet 'Required Fuel - Regular Unleaded'; EPA rates it on regular gasoline. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Copied from the card research (aspiration): Honda's 2022 Civic Sedan launch release, 'a naturally aspirated 2.0-liter (LX and Sport) or a turbocharged 1.5-liter (EX and Touring)'. Same 1,996 cc, 158-hp engine on the 2024 LX sheet with no turbocharger. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.
Copied from the card research: Honda's sheet gives 1,996 cc, marketed as 2.0-liter; EPA lists 2.0 L. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.
Copied from the card research: in-line 4-cylinder; EPA listing also shows 4 cyl. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.
Copied from the card research: '158 hp @ 6,500 rpm (SAE net)', LX and Sport. The 2025 LX changed to a 150-hp engine; that does not apply here. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Card research quotes Honda's 2024 sheet: '158 hp @ 6,500 rpm (SAE net)'. In this session Autopadre's trim tables list 158 hp at 6,500 rpm for the 2022-2024 Civic LX and Sport CVT, and another summary repeats 'makes 158 hp @ 6500 rpm' for the 2024 LX. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.
Copied from the card research: '138 lb-ft @ 4,200 rpm (SAE net)'; also on Honda Information Center's 2024 LX sheet. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Honda gives a single peak-torque speed, '138 lb-ft @ 4,200 rpm' (card research quoting the 2024 sheet); Autopadre lists the same 4,200 rpm for 2022-2024 LX/Sport. Recorded as both low and high because no range is published. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.
Same single-point figure as torqueRpmLow: '138 lb-ft @ 4,200 rpm'. Honda publishes no plateau, so the upper end equals the peak speed. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Copied from the card research, which read '10.8:1 compression' from the LX/Sport engine column of Honda's 2024 Civic Sedan spec sheet. A search in this session did not re-confirm it (that result found 10.8:1 only for an unrelated B16B engine), so it rests on the card research alone. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Copied from the card research: Honda's 2022 launch material says the 2.0-liter 'powers the front wheels through a Continuously Variable Transmission'; Edmunds' 2024 LX page lists front-wheel drive. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Copied from the card research: Honda's sheet identifies the LX/Sport unit as its M-CVT (turbo trims use the LL-CVT); EPA lists 'Automatic (variable gear ratios)'. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

CVT, so these are the two ends of the ratio range, lowest (launch) ratio first, not discrete gears: Honda Information Center's 2024 Civic Sedan page lists the LX/Sport M-CVT 'ratio range of about 2.526 to 0.408', reverse 2.706 to 1.552. Auto123's 2024 EX CVT listing (Canadian EX, 2.0L) gives 2.53 to 0.41. A second Honda table labelled LL-CVT (2.645 to 0.405) belongs to the 1.5-turbo trims; see conflicts. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Honda Information Center's 2024 Civic Sedan page: M-CVT (LX and Sport) final drive 3.941. Auto123's 2024 EX CVT (2.0L) listing gives a 3.94 axle ratio; Road & Track's spec data and Autoblog's 2024 Sport listing also show 3.94. The LL-CVT table's 3.238 is the 1.5-turbo trims'. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Honda's 2024 Civic Sedan feature guide: LX tires 'are 215/55 R16 all-season' on 16-inch steel wheels with covers. The 93H load/speed rating is from iSeeCars ('215/55R16 93H'); Goodyear's and Firestone's 2024 LX Sedan fitment pages also list 215/55R16 (Firestone: H, 32 psi front and rear). Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Square fitment: same 215/55 R16 all-season size front and rear per Honda's LX feature guide; 93H rating from iSeeCars; Firestone lists 32 psi front and rear. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.
Honda's 2024 Civic Sedan feature guide describes the LX tires as '215/55 R16 all-season'. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Honda Information Center's 2024 Civic Sedan table: 'Steering Ratio 11.3 : 1 | 11.5 : 1 | 11.3 : 1 | 11.5 : 1' in the order LX, Sport, EX, Touring, so LX = 11.3:1 (about 2.2-2.3 turns lock-to-lock). The summary warned the column headers were not fully captured, so the LX mapping rests on the column order; Honda's 2025 sedan spec release shows the same split for LX and Sport. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Honda Information Center's 2024 Civic Sedan table: 'Turning Diameter, Curb-to-Curb 36.1 ft | 38.1 ft | 36.1 ft | 38.1 ft' (LX, Sport, EX, Touring). CarEdge's 2024 Civic LX sedan page gives 'Turning radius 18.05'', consistent with 36.1 ft for the LX. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Copied from the card research (brakesFront): 'Power-assisted ventilated disc, 11.1 in', same across LX, Sport, EX and Touring; Honda's 2024 trim comparison repeats 11.1 in / 10.2 in. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Copied from the card research (brakesRear): 'Power-assisted solid disc, 10.2 in'; a parts-fitment listing gives a 10.24 in (260 mm) rear rotor for the 2024 LX. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Copied from the card research: 2024 Honda Civic 4Dr, 2.0 L 4-cyl, Automatic (variable gear ratios), EPA vehicle ID 47071, 35 mpg combined; Honda's 2024 pricing release shows LX 31/40/35. The Sport's AV-S7 listing (30/37/33) is a different rating. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.
Copied from the card research: same EPA listing (ID 47071), 31 mpg city. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.
Copied from the card research: same EPA listing (ID 47071), 40 mpg highway. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Copied from the card research (zeroToSixtySec): Consumer Reports measured 9.7 s 0-60 mph on its Civic SPORT sedan (2022 test car carried on CR's 2022-2024 Civic pages) with the same 158-hp 2.0L, CVT and FWD as the LX, but on 18-inch wheels and about 58 lb heavier (Honda: Sport 2,935 lb vs LX 2,877 lb). This session's search again found 'Consumer Reports clocked 9.7 seconds from 0 to 60 mph for the 158-hp 2.0-liter'. Whether CR subtracts a one-foot rollout was not stated in any result, so testRollout is left blank. No Car and Driver, MotorTrend or Edmunds test of a 2.0-liter 11th-generation sedan surfaced (their tests were of the 1.5-turbo Touring). Paywalled page. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

conflicts.note: Kept 2,877 lb (Honda 2024 sedan spec sheet LX column; Edmunds, J.D. Power, Honda Information Center agree). 2,928 lb (a cars.com 'LX' page and KBB, which mix in the hatchback), 3,054 lb (Yahoo buyer's guide, trim unspecified), 2,895 lb (Auto123, Canadian LX-B) and 2,875 lb (Honda's later-model-year tables) belong to other body styles, trims, markets or years. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.
Kept 184.0 in (Honda 2024 sedan specifications; TrueDelta agrees). Yahoo's 179.0 in covers sedan and hatchback together and matches the hatchback. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Kept 60.9 in (iSeeCars 2024, Auto123 2025 LX). Cars.com's 2024 LX page rounds to 61 in; auto-data's 60.47 in is the Civic Si. A cars.com Sport Touring page showing a 56 in front track is evidently wrong and was ignored. No Honda track figure surfaced. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Kept 5.3 in (CarEdge 2024 LX; consistent with Honda Canada's 2022 sedan 134 mm no-load). AutoPadre's 4.8 in matches the Type R figure; Auto123's 4.4 in has an unclear trim. All aggregator-sourced. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Kept the M-CVT range 2.526-0.408 (Honda Information Center, LX and Sport). The LL-CVT table on the same Honda page (2.645-0.405, reverse 1.859-1.265) is the 1.5-turbo EX/Touring transmission, per the card research's note that Honda's sheet assigns the M-CVT to LX/Sport. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.
Kept 3.941 (Honda M-CVT, LX/Sport; Auto123, Road & Track and Autoblog give 3.94). 3.238 is the LL-CVT (1.5-turbo) final drive. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Kept 36.1 ft for the LX per the column order of Honda's 2024 table (LX 36.1, Sport 38.1, EX 36.1, Touring 38.1) and CarEdge's 18.05 ft LX radius. Yahoo's and AOL's buyer's guides give a single 38.1 ft for 'the standard sedan'. The same split applies to steeringRatio (LX 11.3:1 kept; 11.5:1 is Sport/Touring). Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Kept Honda's 10.2 in solid rear disc. One search summary of a cars.com LX page read 'drum'; a later summary of the same site read disc front and rear, and every Honda source lists rear discs. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Kept 9.7 s (Consumer Reports, measured, Civic Sport 2.0L CVT). 9.5 s (with 17.4 s quarter mile and 112 mph) is a carindigo table with no named tester; 8.27 s (LX) and 8.68 s (Sport) are MotorMatchup simulations; about 8.5 s is an Autobytel pre-launch expectation. None is an instrumented test, so the quarter-mile figures were not recorded. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Not recorded. 126 mph is Yahoo's buyer's guide for 'the 2024 Honda Civic' generally; 127 mph is a MotorMatchup simulation for the LX CVT; 112 mph is carindigo's 'quarter mile top speed' column (a trap speed, not a top speed). No Honda figure or instrumented top-speed run was found, and nothing says whether it is governed. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.
